hero.title: Group chat that fits in your
hero.subtitle: Obelisk on Android, iOS and any modern mobile browser. NIP-29 channels, voice with SFU, encrypted DMs and Lightning zaps. All backed by your Nostr keys: no email, no password.

shot1.title: Discord-style server list, mobile-first
shot1.alt: Obelisk mobile home, with server icons up top, then categorized channels: General Chat, Publications (Finances, Bitcoin, RUNSTR), Voice Channel, Feedback, Uncategorized.
shot1.desc: Your relays show up as servers. Inside each, channels are grouped into the categories the operator publishes (general chat, publications, voice, anything you want), with unread badges and live indicators just like Discord.
shot1.features: Pinned server rail at the top|Operator-controlled categories|Publications nested under their parent|Live indicators on active voice channels

shot2.title: Voice and video that scales past mesh
shot2.alt: Obelisk mobile voice channel running in SFU mode with a test peer transmitting an SMPTE color-bar video stream.
shot2.desc: Small rooms run as a P2P mesh signaled over Nostr (kind 25050). Big-room voice channels route through a mediasoup SFU the channel admin picks, so a room scales to dozens of participants with the same controls.
shot2.features: Mesh for up to 4 people, SFU channels for big rooms|Mute, deafen, screen-share and chat from one bar|Bottom nav stays put while you talk

shot3.title: No email, no password, three ways to log in
shot3.alt: Obelisk mobile login modal showing three options: NIP-46 remote signer, generate a new key, and import an existing nsec.
shot3.desc: Pick the signer that matches your habits: a remote bunker via NIP-46 (Amber, nsec.app), generate a brand-new key on device, or paste an nsec you already own. Onboarding is one screen.
shot3.features: NIP-46 bunker via QR or URL|Generate-and-back-up flow for new users|Paste your existing nsec - your keys, your account

shot4.title: Your Nostr profile, your settings
shot4.alt: Obelisk mobile profile screen: banner, avatar, npub and hex pubkey, Edit Nostr Profile button, Disconnect button and a Preferences tab.
shot4.desc: The same kind 0 profile every Nostr client uses: display name, banner, bio, NIP-05, Lightning address. Edit it once and every Nostr app sees the change.
shot4.features: Copy npub or hex pubkey with one tap|Share a public link to your profile|Per-device preferences kept in localStorage

cta.heading: Take Obelisk with you
cta.subtitle: Open the web app on your phone, install it from the browser menu, and you're done. No app store, no review, no platform tax.

hero.title: A Discord-class workspace, on the open
hero.subtitle: Obelisk in your browser: server rail, categorized channels, publications, member list, mediasoup-powered voice rooms, encrypted DMs and Lightning zaps, all on relays you control.

shot1.title: Three-pane chat, member list and reactions
shot1.alt: Obelisk desktop view of the public General Chat: server rail, channel list, central message stream with reactions and a link preview, and the right-side member list.
shot1.desc: The familiar Discord layout (server rail, channel list, message stream, member sidebar) wired straight to NIP-29 events on the relay. Every message is a signed Nostr event: no backend, no proprietary format.
shot1.features: Replies, reactions and rich link previews|Member list reflects the relay's NIP-29 roster live|Lightning zap any message via NIP-57 + NWC

shot2.title: Publications for slower, deeper conversations
shot2.alt: Obelisk desktop publications view of plaza-publica: four publications (Politica y Economia, But why?, Only-Claws, Finanzas-Trading v2) with OP, message count and last reply time.
shot2.desc: Publication-kind channels turn into a tidy feed: a list of posts, OP and last-reply metadata, each with its own chat, and the same NIP-29 moderation as every other channel.
shot2.features: One-click 'New publication' to start a topic|Each card shows its message count and last reply|Same admin model: removals live on the relay

shot3.title: Big voice rooms with mediasoup and screen share
shot3.alt: Obelisk desktop voice channel in SFU mode showing a test peer streaming an SMPTE color-bar test pattern with the chat sidebar and voice controls.
shot3.desc: Small voice channels are a P2P mesh; big-room voice channels route through a mediasoup SFU the channel admin picks. Same UI, just more people and screen share without melting CPUs.
shot3.features: Pick the SFU per channel, or host your own|Camera and screen share in every room|Mesh signaling rides on Nostr, no sticky-session backend

cta.heading: Open Obelisk in any browser
cta.subtitle: It's a frontend with no signup and no backend of its own. Open it locally, install the PWA, or self-host the build. Same client either way.
